## Scope and documented goal
Found on PR #122 head cce917969c1ee5c12432668e9d996ff9df14bd83; this is a source-backed defect in the proposed opt-in conflict implementation, not a claim about the released version.

[ARCHITECTURE.md](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-vcs/blob/cce917969c1ee5c12432668e9d996ff9df14bd83/ARCHITECTURE.md#L659-L671) says structural disagreements require explicit reconciliation and are never silently recorded as resolved. The [canonical feature](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-vcs/blob/cce917969c1ee5c12432668e9d996ff9df14bd83/.agents/pm/features/pm-vcs-p7objects.toon) requires durable alternatives and preserved independent edits.

## Defect and impact
The [new refusal predicate](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-vcs/blob/cce917969c1ee5c12432668e9d996ff9df14bd83/engine/repo.ts#L2015-L2017) accepts a reported conflict whenever its resulting path has any conflict IDs. It does not establish that those IDs represent this disagreement.

[mergeTrees](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-vcs/blob/cce917969c1ee5c12432668e9d996ff9df14bd83/engine/rewrite.ts#L330-L356) retains our entry for delete/edit and mode disagreements. If that entry already contains an unresolved field/text unit, the predicate accepts the old metadata. The subsequent [commit/HEAD publication](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-vcs/blob/cce917969c1ee5c12432668e9d996ff9df14bd83/engine/repo.ts#L2040-L2050) has no structural-disagreement representation. Resolving the older unit can therefore remove the remaining durable signal while the deletion or mode choice was never reconciled.

## Sanitized reproduction and observed result
Executed the exact pinned mergeTrees function with in-memory tree adapters, followed by the exact refusal predicate:
- Base: path f, payload base, mode 100644, stable file identity
- Ours: payload ours, mode 100644, with an existing unresolved unit
- Theirs: path absent; separately, payload theirs and mode 100755
- Both sides differ from base

Actual: mergeTrees reports content/mode conflicts, preserves the existing unit, and the new structural-refusal predicate evaluates false in both cases.
Expected: unsupported_recorded_conflict before publishing the merge.

Negative controls removing the existing unit make the predicate correctly evaluate true in both cases.

## Method and limits
The merge function and predicate were executed unchanged with in-memory I/O adapters; commit publication consequences are established by the linked call path, not by a full Repository integration run. No production repository was changed. An end-to-end branch scenario remains to be added.

## Acceptance/regression criteria
- Full Repository.merge tests for delete/edit and mode conflicts where ours already carries a recorded field or hunk unit
- With recordConflicts enabled, refuse unsupported structural disagreements regardless of unrelated existing units; HEAD/index/worktree remain unchanged
- Retain the current ordinary field/hunk recording behavior and the no-existing-unit negative controls

All-status issues (122 entries across two REST pages), current PR discussions/reviews, and the canonical feature were checked. Closed #26 concerns older default marker/fail-on-conflict behavior and is distinct.
